# OTA-PRECISION-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog OTA meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VINP VINN VOUT VDD VSS IBIAS` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.

# Public measurement contract: OTA-PRECISION-SKY130

These methods and selected spec.json limits are implementation requirements.
Native validation is not implied by this document or an offline test result.
No method refers to a DUT-internal node or device role. A follower window is not
independent ICMR or distortion-qualified output swing.

## DC, ports and operating point

Connect output to VINN externally, VINP to the input source, CL to external ground.
Meter all six DUT ports with zero-volt sources pointing INTO DUT. Save voltages,
signed currents, KCL residual and the sum of VSS-relative terminal powers.
An ideal output clamp must not create a false operating point. IREF is noiseless,
AC zero, constant in supply-ripple tests and enters IBIAS from VSS.

Sweep the card's input interval at 5 mV spacing, including both endpoints. Retain
all samples; take maximum absolute follower error and maximum signed-port power
only when every required sample is valid. Input loading and IBIAS compliance also
apply at every DC point. Save the independently solved output at all step endpoints.
Device diagnostics are optional; their absence is not a functional failure.
A native DC solution alone is not proof of temporal stability.

## External-loop return ratio

Keep DC feedback and the real CL. e is the inverting-input side and f the output
side. Probe V(e)-V(f) with a DC-zero voltage source; inject DC-zero current from
VSS to e. Run voltage injection (V=1, I=0) and current injection (V=0, I=1) in one
ngspice process. Normalize actual source phasors and use i_f=-I(Vprobe):

A=i_f/Iinj and C=V(e,VSS)/Iinj in the current run;
B=i_f/Vinj and D=V(e,VSS)/Vinj in the voltage run.

L = [2(AD-BC)-A+D] / [2(BC-AD)+A-D+1].

Use the 1+L sign convention, not an automatically sign-flipped curve. Preserve
both raw paths and identical frequency grids/DC/model realization. Numerical
denominator cancellation uses the prescribed relative guard 1e-10; unresolved
values cannot become infinite gain or a passing margin. Record the ratio of
absolute denominator to the sum of its term magnitudes.

Sweep 10 Hz-1 GHz at 50 points/decade for SKY130. All samples finite,
frequencies increasing, endpoint relative error <=1e-7 and log10 spacing
<=0.020001. Low-frequency gain is 20 log10(abs(L)) at 10 Hz, not an invented DC
limit. Reuse all-crossing extraction: interpolate linearly in log frequency,
select the first positive-to-negative 0 dB crossing, unwrap phase from the first
principal phase with adjacent changes within +/-180 degrees. Report each unity
crossing's frequency, unwrapped phase and gain direction, plus touches/boundaries.
Record whether any later sample exceeds 0 dB + 1e-6 dB after the selected crossing.
These diagnostics have no PASS/MISS verdict. Do not
convert the crossing phase into a phase margin or report a gain-margin scalar.
Only the 10 Hz gain and first descending crossing frequency are scored here.
A missing selected crossing cannot pass the bandwidth requirement. Invalid or incomplete
AC data remains a measurement failure.

This two-port measurement is an external-loop metric. It does not certify every
internal feedback mode of an arbitrary circuit. Time-domain requirements remain
separate; global internal-mode certification is not a new acceptance gate.
Method basis: Tian et al., Fig. 7 and eqs. 21-23/30,
https://kenkundert.com/docs/cd2001-01.pdf .

## CMRR: bounded DC balance, then two AC paths

Fix average input to the card's VCM and target VOUT=VCM. Set
VINP=VCM+VD0/2 and VINN=VCM-VD0/2 without output clamp or AC servo.
Try VD0=0 first. Success means abs(VOUT-VCM)<=10 uV at a valid OP. Otherwise
try endpoints -10 mV and +10 mV. Accept an endpoint meeting tolerance or require
a negative/positive residual bracket in that order. Bisect at most 32 times,
retaining each VD0, VOUT and status. There are at most 35 explicit OP commands.
Failure to bracket/converge is NO_VALID_BALANCED_OP / BALANCE_UNRESOLVED, not
proof of topology infeasibility. No adaptive range expansion or silent bias fix.

At the successful unclamped OP keep VD0 fixed. Differential AC is +0.5/-0.5 V
(unit difference); common AC is +1/+1 V (unit common mode). Other sources are AC
zero. At exactly 1 kHz, report 20 log10(abs(Ad/Acm)), the input phasors and both
paths. Zero/underflow/nonfinite ratios or a missing valid OP are invalid evidence,
not automatic infinite rejection.

Perform the bounded control loop and both AC paths in ONE native process and log
explicit OP count and implicit AC operating-point work. Timeout stops that case;
no unlimited loop or free process retries. The offline callback is an algorithm
oracle, not permission to count 35 separate processes as one. The official ngspice
control tutorial documents alter/op/loop flows and multiple analyses in one run:
https://ngspice.sourceforge.io/ngspice-control-language-tutorial.html .

## Transients

Use card-specific levels, edge start/duration, stop time and maximum sample gap.
Each transient uses its own independently solved DC endpoints. Measure slew from
edge start: an output which crosses 20/80% during the finite input edge remains
valid. Require complete finite increasing samples throughout the observation.
Edges start at 1 us, take 10 ns and have 20 us post-edge observation.
The maximum sample gap is 1 ns, divided by four for numerical refinement.
Full verification uses 138 public plus 72 independent cases.

Settling is final interpolated entry that remains within 1% of INPUT step amplitude
about the independently solved destination DC OUTPUT, measured from edge start.
DC tracking is a separate required check. Wrong static levels therefore cannot
pass by tail normalization. Complete unsettled data yields null settling and an
observation-time lower bound; a bound beyond the limit is MISS. Short or missing
waveforms are invalid, not fast settling. Small-step overshoot is excursion beyond
target divided by absolute independent DC output transition. Large-step slew uses
the first ordered direction-correct 20/80% crossings after the edge starts. Retain
recrossings and characterize large-step overshoot; don't add a new waveform score.

## Noise, PSRR and verdicts

Noise uses the real follower at VCM and the same-circuit signal transfer. Save
input-referred ASD, integrate its squared PSD in linear frequency with trapezoids
and boundary interpolation, then square root: 10 Hz-100 kHz at 50 points/decade.
Keep 10/100/1000 Hz lower-cutoff integrals as diagnostics.

PSRR uses two AC paths at the same follower OP: VDD=1/input=0 then VDD=0/input=1.
IREF and VCM do not follow supply ripple. Save phasors and calculate
20 log10(abs(Hsignal/Hsupply)) at 1 kHz and 1 MHz, not an LDO supply/output-only
formula. Invalid/zero transfers do not become favorable zero noise/infinite PSRR.

All required standard cases must produce valid passing metrics on one DUT.
Inclusive limits are compared without rounding. Keep failed metrics and unknowns;
partial execution is not a completed PASS or a substituted last-good design.
Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.
# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VDD.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VDD.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

## Public measurement options

| Analysis | PVT | Load (F) | Cases | Included native measurements |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| nominal | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-12 | 7 | dc, loop, small_up, small_down, large_up, large_down, noise |
| nominal | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 5e-12 | 7 | dc, loop, small_up, small_down, large_up, large_down, noise |
| dc | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-12 | 1 | dc |
| dc | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 5e-12 | 1 | dc |
| loop | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-12 | 1 | loop |
| loop | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 5e-12 | 1 | loop |
| step | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-12 | 5 | dc, small_up, small_down, large_up, large_down |
| step | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 5e-12 | 5 | dc, small_up, small_down, large_up, large_down |
| noise | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 2e-12 | 1 | noise |
| noise | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 5e-12 | 1 | noise |
| psrr | N, SLH, FHC | 2e-12 | 1 | psrr |
| psrr | N, SLH, FHC | 5e-12 | 1 | psrr |
| cmrr | N, SLH, FHC | 2e-12 | 1 | cmrr |
| cmrr | N, SLH, FHC | 5e-12 | 1 | cmrr |

Defaults and seed requirements:

- nominal: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-12 F. No seed accepted.
- dc: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-12 F. No seed accepted.
- loop: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-12 F. No seed accepted.
- step: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-12 F. No seed accepted.
- noise: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-12 F. No seed accepted.
- psrr: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-12 F. No seed accepted.
- cmrr: omitted `--cl` uses 2e-12 F. No seed accepted.

One native case is one simulator process. Bundled internal analyses are retained in evidence.
`estimate` returns the exact case plan without launching a solver. Independent evaluation conditions are not available to participants.

The task calls for an independent analog design with no seed circuit. I’m starting with a two-stage, Miller-compensated CMOS OTA: a differential input pair for gain and common-mode rejection, with bias currents derived from IBIAS and a separate PMOS bias branch for the output stage. I’ll validate the netlist before spending measurement cases.

XTAIL NTAIL IBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=4 l=1 m=1
XINN NDIFFP VINN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20 l=2 m=1
XINP NDIFFN VINP NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20 l=2 m=1
XLOAD1 NDIFFP NDIFFP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=20 l=2 m=1
XLOAD2 NDIFFN NDIFFP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=20 l=2 m=1
* Resistor-set PMOS reference and second gain stage
XPREF VBP VBP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=10 l=2 m=1
RBP VBP VSS 270k
XPOUT VOUT VBP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=20 l=2 m=1
XGAIN VOUT NDIFFN VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=1 l=3 m=1
* Miller compensation with a series zero-nulling resistor
CCOMP NDIFFN NCOMP 100f
RCOMP NCOMP VOUT 22k
.ends DUT
EOF

MODEL

The first full bundle exposed a stability failure: although DC and low frequency gain pass, all step responses are still moving at 20 µs and overshoot badly. I’m increasing the Miller capacitor to lower crossover frequency, then I’ll remeasure the complete bundle and tune input sizing for the small noise miss.

MODEL

With the larger capacitor, the waveform settles within a microsecond, but overshoot remains far above 10%, and the unity crossing phase is still too lagged. I’ll add more phase lead through the Miller series resistor while keeping enough bandwidth for the 1 MHz requirement.

MODEL

Widening the input pair brought integrated noise below its limit. The current compensation still leaves excessive small-step overshoot, so I’m reducing the series resistance to make the Miller capacitor act more strongly at crossover; then I’ll recheck bandwidth, settling, and noise together.

MODEL

The best compensation point so far settles quickly and passes the downward overshoot and noise checks, but the rising step still overshoots heavily. I’m raising the output-stage bias current and scaling its NMOS sink with it, which should improve pull-up drive and move the output pole higher.

* Resistor-set PMOS bias for the second gain stage
XPREF VBP VBP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=10 l=2 m=1

.ends DUT

MODEL

The source-follower variant improves the transient, but it loses too much low-frequency gain and has a large nominal tracking offset, so I’m returning to the two-stage design. I’ll tune the Miller resistor around the stable region and then test the 5 pF load and the required supply/process corners.

MODEL

The two-stage design still cannot meet the rising-step overshoot limit. I’m trying a complementary CMOS output stage driven from the differential pair’s first-stage node, so the PMOS can actively source current as the NMOS turns off; this should reduce the output-stage asymmetry.

cat > dut.spice <<'EOF'
.subckt DUT VINP VINN VOUT VDD VSS IBIAS
* IBIAS-referenced NMOS differential pair with PMOS mirror load
XREFN IBIAS IBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=4 l=1 m=1
XTAIL NTAIL IBIAS VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=4 l=1 m=1
XINN NDIFFP VINN NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=40 l=2 m=1
XINP NDIFFN VINP NTAIL VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=40 l=2 m=1
XLOAD1 NDIFFP NDIFFP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=20 l=2 m=1
XLOAD2 NDIFFN NDIFFP VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=20 l=2 m=1
* Complementary common-source output stage
XOUTN VOUT NDIFFN VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=2 l=3 m=1
XOUTP VOUT NDIFFN VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=30 l=3 m=1
* Miller compensation with a series phase-lead resistor
CCOMP NDIFFN NCOMP 2.7p
RCOMP NCOMP VOUT 10k
.ends DUT

The current netlist passes the nominal bundle at both load limits. I’m measuring the same design at every remaining slow and fast condition, at 2 pF and 5 pF, to identify any corner-dependent failures before submission.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json, subprocess, sys
pvts = [\"SLC\", \"SLH\", \"SHC\", \"SHH\", \"FLC\", \"FLH\", \"FHC\", \"FHH\"]
for pvt in pvts:
    for cl in (2e-12, 5e-12):
        experiment_id = f\"grid_{pvt}_{'2p' if cl == 2e-12 else '5p'}\"
        request = {\"action\":\"measure\", \"experiment_id\":experiment_id, \"analysis\":\"nominal\", \"pvt\":pvt, \"cl\":cl}
        with open(\"REQUEST.json\", \"w\") as f:
            json.dump(request, f)
        p = subprocess.run([\"atb-client\", \"--request\", \"REQUEST.json\"], text=True, capture_output=True)
        try:
            d = json.loads(p.stdout)
        except Exception:
            print(json.dumps({\"experiment_id\":experiment_id,\"returncode\":p.returncode,\"error\":p.stderr[-1000:],\"stdout\":p.stdout[-1000:]}), flush=True)
            continue
        table = d.get(\"summary\",{}).get(\"spec_table\",[])
        misses = [{k:r.get(k) for k in (\"metric\",\"measured\",\"limit\",\"verdict\",\"case_id\")} for r in table if r.get(\"verdict\") "'!= "PASS"]
        statuses = [{"case_id":c.get("case_id"),"status":c.get("status")} for c in d.get("cases",[])]
        print(json.dumps({"experiment_id":experiment_id,"revision":d.get("revision"),"misses":misses,"case_statuses":statuses,"budget":d.get("budget",{}).get("remaining_seconds")}), flush=True)
PY'
MODEL

The slow cold corner is a major exception: nominal tracking and stability shift badly there, while the slow hot corner is only slightly outside tracking and noise. The remaining corner measurements are still running; I’ll use them to see whether the issue is limited to slow cold or affects other corners too.

The wider pair improves nominal tracking, but it does not solve the cold low-supply error and it worsens tracking at several hot corners. I’m comparing the earlier resistor-biased output stage against this complementary stage, since its supply and temperature dependence may be easier to balance across the full grid.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json, subprocess
pvts = [\"SLC\", \"SLH\", \"SHC\", \"SHH\", \"FLC\", \"FLH\", \"FHC\", \"FHH\"]
for pvt in pvts:
    for cl in (2e-12, 5e-12):
        experiment_id=f\"grid2_{pvt}_{'2p' if cl==2e-12 else '5p'}\"
        request={\"action\":\"measure\",\"experiment_id\":experiment_id,\"analysis\":\"nominal\",\"pvt\":pvt,\"cl\":cl}
        with open(\"REQUEST.json\",\"w\") as f: json.dump(request,f)
        p=subprocess.run([\"atb-client\",\"--request\",\"REQUEST.json\"],text=True,capture_output=True)
        try: d=json.loads(p.stdout)
        except Exception:
            print(json.dumps({\"experiment_id\":experiment_id,\"error\":p.stderr[-700:],\"stdout\":p.stdout[-700:]}),flush=True); continue
        table=d.get(\"summary\",{}).get(\"spec_table\",[])
        misses=[{k:r.get(k) for k in (\"metric\",\"measured\",\"limit\",\"verdict\",\"case_id\")} for r in table if r.get(\"verdict\")"'!="PASS"]
        statuses=[{"case_id":c.get("case_id"),"status":c.get("status")} for c in d.get("cases",[])]
        print(json.dumps({"experiment_id":experiment_id,"misses":misses,"case_statuses":statuses,"remaining_seconds":d.get("budget",{}).get("remaining_seconds")}),flush=True)
PY'
MODEL

Slow hot and slow high-supply conditions pass both loads, but slow cold remains unstable and over the tracking limit. I’m continuing through the fast corners to confirm whether the remaining problem is specifically cold behavior or low supply more generally.

# OTA-PRECISION-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog OTA meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VINP VINN VOUT VDD VSS IBIAS` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.
# Public measurement contract: OTA-PRECISION-SKY130

These methods and selected spec.json limits are implementation requirements.
Native validation is not implied by this document or an offline test result.
No method refers to a DUT-internal node or device role. A follower window is not
independent ICMR or distortion-qualified output swing.

## DC, ports and operating point

Connect output to VINN externally, VINP to the input source, CL to external ground.
Meter all six DUT ports with zero-volt sources pointing INTO DUT. Save voltages,
signed currents, KCL residual and the sum of VSS-relative terminal powers.
An ideal output clamp must not create a false operating point. IREF is noiseless,
AC zero, constant in supply-ripple tests and enters IBIAS from VSS.

Sweep the card's input interval at 5 mV spacing, including both endpoints. Retain
all samples; take maximum absolute follower error and maximum signed-port power
only when every required sample is valid. Input loading and IBIAS compliance also
apply at every DC point. Save the independently solved output at all step endpoints.
Device diagnostics are optional; their absence is not a functional failure.
A native DC solution alone is not proof of temporal stability.

## External-loop return ratio

Keep DC feedback and the real CL. e is the inverting-input side and f the output
side. Probe V(e)-V(f) with a DC-zero voltage source; inject DC-zero current from
VSS to e. Run voltage injection (V=1, I=0) and current injection (V=0, I=1) in one
ngspice process. Normalize actual source phasors and use i_f=-I(Vprobe):

A=i_f/Iinj and C=V(e,VSS)/Iinj in the current run;
B=i_f/Vinj and D=V(e,VSS)/Vinj in the voltage run.

L = [2(AD-BC)-A+D] / [2(BC-AD)+A-D+1].

Use the 1+L sign convention, not an automatically sign-flipped curve. Preserve
both raw paths and identical frequency grids/DC/model realization. Numerical
denominator cancellation uses the prescribed relative guard 1e-10; unresolved
values cannot become infinite gain or a passing margin. Record the ratio of
absolute denominator to the sum of its term magnitudes.

Sweep 10 Hz-1 GHz at 50 points/decade for SKY130. All samples finite,
frequencies increasing, endpoint relative error <=1e-7 and log10 spacing
<=0.020001. Low-frequency gain is 20 log10(abs(L)) at 10 Hz, not an invented DC
limit. Reuse all-crossing extraction: interpolate linearly in log frequency,
select the first positive-to-negative 0 dB crossing, unwrap phase from the first
principal phase with adjacent changes within +/-180 degrees. Report each unity
crossing's frequency, unwrapped phase and gain direction, plus touches/boundaries.
Record whether any later sample exceeds 0 dB + 1e-6 dB after the selected crossing.
These diagnostics have no PASS/MISS verdict. Do not
convert the crossing phase into a phase margin or report a gain-margin scalar.
Only the 10 Hz gain and first descending crossing frequency are scored here.
A missing selected crossing cannot pass the bandwidth requirement. Invalid or incomplete
AC data remains a measurement failure.

This two-port measurement is an external-loop metric. It does not certify every
internal feedback mode of an arbitrary circuit. Time-domain requirements remain
separate; global internal-mode certification is not a new acceptance gate.
Method basis: Tian et al., Fig. 7 and eqs. 21-23/30,
https://kenkundert.com/docs/cd2001-01.pdf .

## CMRR: bounded DC balance, then two AC paths

Fix average input to the card's VCM and target VOUT=VCM. Set
VINP=VCM+VD0/2 and VINN=VCM-VD0/2 without output clamp or AC servo.
Try VD0=0 first. Success means abs(VOUT-VCM)<=10 uV at a valid OP. Otherwise
try endpoints -10 mV and +10 mV. Accept an endpoint meeting tolerance or require
a negative/positive residual bracket in that order. Bisect at most 32 times,
retaining each VD0, VOUT and status. There are at most 35 explicit OP commands.
Failure to bracket/converge is NO_VALID_BALANCED_OP / BALANCE_UNRESOLVED, not
proof of topology infeasibility. No adaptive range expansion or silent bias fix.

At the successful unclamped OP keep VD0 fixed. Differential AC is +0.5/-0.5 V
(unit difference); common AC is +1/+1 V (unit common mode). Other sources are AC
zero. At exactly 1 kHz, report 20 log10(abs(Ad/Acm)), the input phasors and both
paths. Zero/underflow/nonfinite ratios or a missing valid OP are invalid evidence,
not automatic infinite rejection.

Perform the bounded control loop and both AC paths in ONE native process and log
explicit OP count and implicit AC operating-point work. Timeout stops that case;
no unlimited loop or free process retries. The offline callback is an algorithm
oracle, not permission to count 35 separate processes as one. The official ngspice
control tutorial documents alter/op/loop flows and multiple analyses in one run:
https://ngspice.sourceforge.io/ngspice-control-language-tutorial.html .

## Transients

Use card-specific levels, edge start/duration, stop time and maximum sample gap.
Each transient uses its own independently solved DC endpoints. Measure slew from
edge start: an output which crosses 20/80% during the finite input edge remains
valid. Require complete finite increasing samples throughout the observation.
Edges start at 1 us, take 10 ns and have 20 us post-edge observation.
The maximum sample gap is 1 ns, divided by four for numerical refinement.
Full verification uses 138 public plus 72 independent cases.

Settling is final interpolated entry that remains within 1% of INPUT step amplitude
about the independently solved destination DC OUTPUT, measured from edge start.
DC tracking is a separate required check. Wrong static levels therefore cannot
pass by tail normalization. Complete unsettled data yields null settling and an
observation-time lower bound; a bound beyond the limit is MISS. Short or missing
waveforms are invalid, not fast settling. Small-step overshoot is excursion beyond
target divided by absolute independent DC output transition. Large-step slew uses
the first ordered direction-correct 20/80% crossings after the edge starts. Retain
recrossings and characterize large-step overshoot; don't add a new waveform score.

## Noise, PSRR and verdicts

Noise uses the real follower at VCM and the same-circuit signal transfer. Save
input-referred ASD, integrate its squared PSD in linear frequency with trapezoids
and boundary interpolation, then square root: 10 Hz-100 kHz at 50 points/decade.
Keep 10/100/1000 Hz lower-cutoff integrals as diagnostics.

PSRR uses two AC paths at the same follower OP: VDD=1/input=0 then VDD=0/input=1.
IREF and VCM do not follow supply ripple. Save phasors and calculate
20 log10(abs(Hsignal/Hsupply)) at 1 kHz and 1 MHz, not an LDO supply/output-only
formula. Invalid/zero transfers do not become favorable zero noise/infinite PSRR.

All required standard cases must produce valid passing metrics on one DUT.
Inclusive limits are compared without rounding. Keep failed metrics and unknowns;
partial execution is not a completed PASS or a substituted last-good design.
Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VDD.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

MODEL

The 10 MΩ symmetric feed reduced SLC tracking error from 3.68 mV to 2.43 mV while keeping input current at 48 nA. That scaling is promising, so I’m testing 1 MΩ at the same cold corners and hot endpoints; it may correct more offset, though I’ll also recheck stability if it works.

for pvt in ['SLC','FLC','SHH','FHH','N']:
    req={'action':'measure','experiment_id':f'trial44_1m_{pvt.lower()}_dc','analysis':'dc','pvt':pvt,'cl':2e-12}
    Path('REQUEST.json').write_text(json.dumps(req))
    r=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','REQUEST.json'],capture_output=True,text=True)
    try: d=json.loads(r.stdout)
    except Exception: print('ERROR',pvt,r.returncode,r.stdout[:500],r.stderr[:500]); continue
    cases=d.get('cases',[])
    m=cases[0].get('measurements',{}) if cases else {}
    pts=m.get('points',[])
    ends=[(round(x['input_v'],3),round(x['output_v']-x['input_v'],6)) for x in [pts[0],pts[-1]]] if len(pts)>=2 else []
    print(pvt,'status',cases[0].get('status') if cases else d.get('ok'),'track',m.get('tracking_max_error_v'),'in',m.get('input_current_abs_a'),'ends',ends,'remain',d.get('budget',{}).get('remaining_seconds'))

MODEL

The resistor feed gives mixed corner behavior. I’m trying a simpler class A output stage next: one NMOS sinks current and a resistor to VDD supplies it. That removes the P/N inverter crossover that appears to be driving much of the temperature shift; the 150 kΩ pullup should still provide enough current for the required slew.

MODEL

The resistor combination improves some corners but still leaves several millivolt scale misses. I’ve started a small valid-value sweep of feed and gate-bias resistors across all nine PVT cases; this should show whether that approach has a useful all-corner setting before I spend more trials on compensation and transient performance.

MODEL

The feed/bias sweep still misses multiple corners, with the worst errors around 2.7–3.5 mV. I’m now changing the PMOS mirror sizing, which sets the first-stage balance point and may correct the corner spread at its source rather than relying on weak bias feeds.

from pathlib import Path
import json,subprocess
base=Path('/tmp/dut_candidate33.spice').read_text().replace('w=40 l=2 m=1','w=80 l=2 m=1').replace('w=45 l=3 m=1','w=60 l=3 m=1')
configs=[(rin,rg) for rin in ['4meg','6meg','8meg'] for rg in ['3meg','5meg','8meg','12meg']]
pvts=['N','SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']
results=[]
for rin,rg in configs:
    tag=rin.replace('meg','m')+'_g'+rg.replace('meg','m')
    s=base.replace('RCOMP NCOMP VOUT 31k','RCOMP NCOMP VOUT 31k\\nRCMINP NDIFFN VINP '+rin+'\\nRCMINN NDIFFN VINN '+rin+'\\nRBIASG NDIFFN VSS '+rg)
    Path('dut.spice').write_text(s)
    val=json.loads(subprocess.run(['atb-client','validate'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
    if not val.get('ok'):
        print('INVALID',tag,val); continue
    row={'tag':tag,'revision':val.get('revision'),'by_pvt':{}}
    for pvt in pvts:
        req={'action':'measure','experiment_id':f'trial68_{tag}_{pvt.lower()}_dc','analysis':'dc','pvt':pvt,'cl':2e-12}
        Path('REQUEST.json').write_text(json.dumps(req)); proc=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','REQUEST.json'],capture_output=True,text=True)
        try:d=json.loads(proc.stdout)
        except Exception: print('ERROR',tag,pvt,proc.returncode,proc.stdout[:200],proc.stderr[:200]); continue
        cs=d.get('cases',[]); m=cs[0].get('measurements',{}) if cs else {}; pts=m.get('points',[])
        row['by_pvt'][pvt]={'track':m.get('tracking_max_error_v'),'ends':[round(x['output_v']-x['input_v'],6) for x in [pts[0],pts[-1]]] if len(pts)>=2 else []}
    row['worst']=max((v['track'] or 0) for v in row['by_pvt'].values()) if row['by_pvt'] else None
    results.append(row); print('CONFIG',tag,'worst',row['worst'],'pvt',sorted(((v['track'] or 0,k) for k,v in row['by_pvt'].items()),reverse=True)[:3])
Path('/tmp/trial68_grid.json').write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2))
print('BEST',min(results,key=lambda x:x['worst']) if results else None)

  print('CONFIG XLOAD2',w,'valid',v.get('ok'),'rev',v.get('revision'))
  worst=[]
  for pvt in ['N','SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']:

    Path('REQUEST.json').write_text(json.dumps(req)); r=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','REQUEST.json'],capture_output=True,text=True); d=json.loads(r.stdout)

    worst.append((t,pvt)); print(pvt,t,e)

MODEL

Changing only the mirror reference size did not help; the next trial adjusts the output mirror ratio around unity while holding the larger mirror and output stage fixed. This can set a small intentional current imbalance that may cancel the remaining input referred offset.

base=Path('/tmp/dut_candidate33.spice').read_text().replace('w=40 l=2 m=1','w=80 l=2 m=1').replace('w=45 l=3 m=1','w=60 l=3 m=1')
base=base.replace('RCOMP NCOMP VOUT 31k','RCOMP NCOMP VOUT 31k\\nRCMINP NDIFFN VINP 100meg\\nRCMINN NDIFFN VINN 4meg\\nRBIASG NDIFFN VSS 9.5meg\\nRTRACK VINP VOUT 1k')
Path('dut.spice').write_text(base)
v=json.loads(subprocess.run(['atb-client','validate'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout); print('VALID',v.get('ok'),v.get('revision'))
for pvt in ['N','SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']:
 req={'action':'measure','experiment_id':f'trial77_rtrack1k_{pvt.lower()}_dc','analysis':'dc','pvt':pvt,'cl':2e-12}
 Path('REQUEST.json').write_text(json.dumps(req)); r=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','REQUEST.json'],capture_output=True,text=True); d=json.loads(r.stdout)
 cs=d.get('cases',[]); m=cs[0].get('measurements',{}) if cs else {}; pts=m.get('points',[]); ends=[round(x['output_v']-x['input_v'],6) for x in [pts[0],pts[-1]]] if len(pts)>=2 else []
 print(pvt,m.get('tracking_max_error_v'),ends,m.get('input_current_abs_a'),d.get('budget',{}).get('remaining_seconds'))
PY"

MODEL

The DC‑optimized sizing and bias network loses too much low frequency return ratio: the nominal measurement reports 59 dB against an 80 dB minimum, although bandwidth and transients pass. I’m separating the sizing and resistor effects now; I won’t use a DC improvement that breaks the required loop gain.

I isolated the problem: the 8.5 MΩ input feeds cause the return ratio to fall from about 95 dB to 59 dB; the gate pull down alone leaves it near 94 dB. I’m testing a much weaker input feed with that gate bias to see if it retains enough loop gain while still helping DC tracking.

MODEL

A 100 MΩ feed keeps the return ratio just over 80 dB but still misses cold tracking, while lower feed resistance violates the gain floor. I’m verifying the larger mirror/output sizing without that feed; it preserves about 95 dB return ratio and is the most promising valid option so far.

MODEL

The larger mirror/output stage without the low resistance input feed passes loop gain, settling, slew and noise at both nominal loads; tracking misses by only 1.3 µV nominally. Its PVT DC spread is still too wide, so I’m testing supply referenced gate bias as a way to shift the cold and hot corners without loading the external loop.

The current candidate passes every nominal metric at 2 pF and 5 pF after increasing the output PMOS to 66 µm; return ratio is about 95 dB and noise is 14.6 µV rms. I’m running the same bundled checks over the full PVT grid now, so the final choice reflects transient stability and AC behavior at the corners too.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 -u - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import json,subprocess
base=Path('/tmp/dut_candidate33.spice').read_text().replace('w=40 l=2 m=1','w=80 l=2 m=1').replace('XOUTP VOUT NDIFFN VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=45 l=3 m=1','XOUTP VOUT NDIFFN VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=66 l=3 m=1')
Path('dut.spice').write_text(base)
v=json.loads(subprocess.run(['atb-client','validate'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout); print('REVISION',v.get('revision'),flush=True)
results=[]
for pvt in ['N','SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']:
 for tag,cl in [('2p',2e-12),('5p',5e-12)]:
  eid=f'trial86_pout66_nominal_{tag}' if pvt=='N' else f'trial92_fullnom_{pvt.lower()}_{tag}'
  req={'action':'measure','experiment_id':eid,'analysis':'nominal','pvt':pvt,'cl':cl}
  Path('REQUEST.json').write_text(json.dumps(req)); proc=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','REQUEST.json'],capture_output=True,text=True)
  try:d=json.loads(proc.stdout)
  except Exception: print('ERROR',pvt,tag,proc.returncode,proc.stdout[:500],proc.stderr[:300],flush=True); continue
  misses=[(x.get('metric'),x.get('measured'),x.get('limit'),x.get('verdict')) for x in d.get('summary',{}).get('spec_table',[]) if x.get('verdict') not in ('PASS',)]
  case_stat=[(c.get('case_id'),c.get('status')) for c in d.get('cases',[])]
  row={'pvt':pvt,'cl':tag,'misses':misses,'cases':case_stat,'remain':d.get('budget',{}).get('remaining_seconds')}; results.append(row)
  print('RESULT',pvt,tag,'misses',misses,'cases',case_stat,'remain',row['remain'],flush=True)
Path('/tmp/trial92_fullnom.json').write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2))

I’m letting the remaining corners finish, then I’ll retune compensation against the cold instability without disturbing the nominal pass.

# OTA-PRECISION-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog OTA meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VINP VINN VOUT VDD VSS IBIAS` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.
# Public measurement contract: OTA-PRECISION-SKY130

These methods and selected spec.json limits are implementation requirements.
Native validation is not implied by this document or an offline test result.
No method refers to a DUT-internal node or device role. A follower window is not
independent ICMR or distortion-qualified output swing.

## DC, ports and operating point

Connect output to VINN externally, VINP to the input source, CL to external ground.
Meter all six DUT ports with zero-volt sources pointing INTO DUT. Save voltages,
signed currents, KCL residual and the sum of VSS-relative terminal powers.
An ideal output clamp must not create a false operating point. IREF is noiseless,
AC zero, constant in supply-ripple tests and enters IBIAS from VSS.

Sweep the card's input interval at 5 mV spacing, including both endpoints. Retain
all samples; take maximum absolute follower error and maximum signed-port power
only when every required sample is valid. Input loading and IBIAS compliance also
apply at every DC point. Save the independently solved output at all step endpoints.
Device diagnostics are optional; their absence is not a functional failure.
A native DC solution alone is not proof of temporal stability.

## External-loop return ratio

Keep DC feedback and the real CL. e is the inverting-input side and f the output
side. Probe V(e)-V(f) with a DC-zero voltage source; inject DC-zero current from
VSS to e. Run voltage injection (V=1, I=0) and current injection (V=0, I=1) in one
ngspice process. Normalize actual source phasors and use i_f=-I(Vprobe):

A=i_f/Iinj and C=V(e,VSS)/Iinj in the current run;
B=i_f/Vinj and D=V(e,VSS)/Vinj in the voltage run.

L = [2(AD-BC)-A+D] / [2(BC-AD)+A-D+1].

Use the 1+L sign convention, not an automatically sign-flipped curve. Preserve
both raw paths and identical frequency grids/DC/model realization. Numerical
denominator cancellation uses the prescribed relative guard 1e-10; unresolved
values cannot become infinite gain or a passing margin. Record the ratio of
absolute denominator to the sum of its term magnitudes.

Sweep 10 Hz-1 GHz at 50 points/decade for SKY130. All samples finite,
frequencies increasing, endpoint relative error <=1e-7 and log10 spacing
<=0.020001. Low-frequency gain is 20 log10(abs(L)) at 10 Hz, not an invented DC
limit. Reuse all-crossing extraction: interpolate linearly in log frequency,
select the first positive-to-negative 0 dB crossing, unwrap phase from the first
principal phase with adjacent changes within +/-180 degrees. Report each unity
crossing's frequency, unwrapped phase and gain direction, plus touches/boundaries.
Record whether any later sample exceeds 0 dB + 1e-6 dB after the selected crossing.
These diagnostics have no PASS/MISS verdict. Do not
convert the crossing phase into a phase margin or report a gain-margin scalar.
Only the 10 Hz gain and first descending crossing frequency are scored here.
A missing selected crossing cannot pass the bandwidth requirement. Invalid or incomplete
AC data remains a measurement failure.

This two-port measurement is an external-loop metric. It does not certify every
internal feedback mode of an arbitrary circuit. Time-domain requirements remain
separate; global internal-mode certification is not a new acceptance gate.
Method basis: Tian et al., Fig. 7 and eqs. 21-23/30,
https://kenkundert.com/docs/cd2001-01.pdf .

## CMRR: bounded DC balance, then two AC paths

Fix average input to the card's VCM and target VOUT=VCM. Set
VINP=VCM+VD0/2 and VINN=VCM-VD0/2 without output clamp or AC servo.
Try VD0=0 first. Success means abs(VOUT-VCM)<=10 uV at a valid OP. Otherwise
try endpoints -10 mV and +10 mV. Accept an endpoint meeting tolerance or require
a negative/positive residual bracket in that order. Bisect at most 32 times,
retaining each VD0, VOUT and status. There are at most 35 explicit OP commands.
Failure to bracket/converge is NO_VALID_BALANCED_OP / BALANCE_UNRESOLVED, not
proof of topology infeasibility. No adaptive range expansion or silent bias fix.

At the successful unclamped OP keep VD0 fixed. Differential AC is +0.5/-0.5 V
(unit difference); common AC is +1/+1 V (unit common mode). Other sources are AC
zero. At exactly 1 kHz, report 20 log10(abs(Ad/Acm)), the input phasors and both
paths. Zero/underflow/nonfinite ratios or a missing valid OP are invalid evidence,
not automatic infinite rejection.

Perform the bounded control loop and both AC paths in ONE native process and log
explicit OP count and implicit AC operating-point work. Timeout stops that case;
no unlimited loop or free process retries. The offline callback is an algorithm
oracle, not permission to count 35 separate processes as one. The official ngspice
control tutorial documents alter/op/loop flows and multiple analyses in one run:
https://ngspice.sourceforge.io/ngspice-control-language-tutorial.html .

## Transients

Use card-specific levels, edge start/duration, stop time and maximum sample gap.
Each transient uses its own independently solved DC endpoints. Measure slew from
edge start: an output which crosses 20/80% during the finite input edge remains
valid. Require complete finite increasing samples throughout the observation.
Edges start at 1 us, take 10 ns and have 20 us post-edge observation.
The maximum sample gap is 1 ns, divided by four for numerical refinement.
Full verification uses 138 public plus 72 independent cases.

Settling is final interpolated entry that remains within 1% of INPUT step amplitude
about the independently solved destination DC OUTPUT, measured from edge start.
DC tracking is a separate required check. Wrong static levels therefore cannot
pass by tail normalization. Complete unsettled data yields null settling and an
observation-time lower bound; a bound beyond the limit is MISS. Short or missing
waveforms are invalid, not fast settling. Small-step overshoot is excursion beyond
target divided by absolute independent DC output transition. Large-step slew uses
the first ordered direction-correct 20/80% crossings after the edge starts. Retain
recrossings and characterize large-step overshoot; don't add a new waveform score.

## Noise, PSRR and verdicts

Noise uses the real follower at VCM and the same-circuit signal transfer. Save
input-referred ASD, integrate its squared PSD in linear frequency with trapezoids
and boundary interpolation, then square root: 10 Hz-100 kHz at 50 points/decade.
Keep 10/100/1000 Hz lower-cutoff integrals as diagnostics.

PSRR uses two AC paths at the same follower OP: VDD=1/input=0 then VDD=0/input=1.
IREF and VCM do not follow supply ripple. Save phasors and calculate
20 log10(abs(Hsignal/Hsupply)) at 1 kHz and 1 MHz, not an LDO supply/output-only
formula. Invalid/zero transfers do not become favorable zero noise/infinite PSRR.

All required standard cases must produce valid passing metrics on one DUT.
Inclusive limits are compared without rounding. Keep failed metrics and unknowns;
partial execution is not a completed PASS or a substituted last-good design.
Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

Bash
# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VDD.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

I’m testing a weak output-to-IBIAS feedback path to make the pull-up bias respond to output level; if it does not improve the corner spread, I’ll revert to the fully nominal-passing candidate and submit that with the corner misses documented.
